items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: FDA seeks input on telesurgery, autonomous robotics
items.summary: Rapid advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning and connectivity are driving expansion of robotic applications in a wide range of clinical settings, the FDA said. Increases in processing power, data storage and computational efficiency are enabling progress in robotic systems with autonomous capabilities. [...] In another example of teleoperation, manufacturers are developing devices that enable technicians to remotely perform ultrasounds, the FDA said. Robotic devices include stereotactic navigation systems, imaging devices and endoluminal navigation devices. [...] The FDA is asking the robotics community to submit comments on the discussion paper by Jan. 5. Ahead of that deadline, a public workshop to discuss the topics raised in the paper is scheduled for Dec. 2-3.

items.title: NVIDIA launches GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL - The Robot Report
items.summary:
Walden Robotics is using Isaac Sim’s photorealistic rendering to train and evaluate its general-purpose robot in virtual environments for manufacturing and logistics. Dexmate is exploring how coding agents can rehearse and refine manipulation strategies in Isaac Sim before executing them on its Vega robot. [...] Robotics developers are already putting NVIDIA’s latest technology to the test. A number of developers are using Isaac Lab 3.0 and Newton. At CoRL, Skild AI announced Scalable Throughput-optimized Engine for Embodied Learning, or STEEL, a new rigid-body physics solver built on Newton to accelerate robot training with Isaac Lab. [...] Nexuni is testing GR00T 2 for robotic laundry. Foxconn is applying GR00T 2 to factory automation for server manufacturing, and Siemens is evaluating it across industrial use cases.

MicroAGI is using GR00T 2, post-trained through reinforcement learning, to perform Ethernet cable swapping with a YAM robotic arm. Its agentic robotics approach automates the creation and calibration of simulation environments using Isaac Lab 3.0 and Newton, where the policy is trained.

result.actual_text:
Để giải phương trình \(x^2 - 4 = 0\), ta có thể viết lại phương trình như sau:

\[
x^2 = 4
\]

Tiếp theo, lấy căn bậc hai của cả hai vế:

\[
x = \pm 2
\]

Vậy nghiệm của phương trình là:

\[
x = 2 \quad \text{hoặc} \quad x = -2
\]

items.title: OpenAI Tries to Ease Backlash Against AI Data Centers
items.summary:
OpenAI is promising to pay for the power costs accrued by its data centers and give communities more say over construction. The list of commitments came two days after midterm election results favored candidates that opposed the data center buildout aimed at supporting the growing artificial intelligence industry.

See Also: Frictionless Security: How AI is Redefining Access in Highly Regulated Industries [...] For enterprise technology leaders, the announcements are a mixed bag. OpenAI is attempting to ensure it has access to the compute it will need to grow by assuaging the concerns of communities that are increasingly saying no to data center expansion, but for businesses that are still trying to formulate their AI strategy, OpenAI's compact doesn't offer much certainty. [...] The compact outlined locally tailored agreements for future OpenAI campuses, community input into development plans and annual public progress reports. OpenAI said it will cover the electricity it consumes and the incremental infrastructure costs required to serve its sites. It will also provide financial assurances before major spending begins to protect other utility customers if a project is delayed, reduced or canceled.

items.title: Top Robotics Stocks With Strong Potential for Long-Term Growth
items.summary: With orders accelerating, humanoid pilots becoming contracts, surgical robotics gaining regulatory clarity and defense autonomy topping budget priorities, U.S. robotics enters 2027 with diversified demand drivers, positioning sector leaders well as adoption scales across factories, hospitals and homes. [...] U.S. robotics stocks enter the final stretch of 2026 on firmer footing, as September through early November brought a wave of commercial deployments, regulatory progress and government funding signals. North American robot orders hit their strongest quarter of the year, humanoids moved from demos toward contracted factory work, the FDA outlined a clearer path for surgical robots, and the Pentagon made autonomy a top budget priority. Together, these developments point to a broadening demand base [...] U.S. robotics demand strengthened through the fall. items.title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future. | MIT Technology Review
items.summary:
With all the human support they need, the robots are closer to radio-controlled cars than Waymos. Many tasks, such as making the bed and folding laundry, require what’s called kinematic guidance: The human pilot performs the necessary motions, and sensors transmit those movements to the robot, which copies them. These kinematically guided tasks produce especially valuable training data. Tau’s AI models might not have solved laundry folding yet, but learning from the examples of robots that have [...] But according to Tau cofounder Cornelia Weinzierl, to whom I came clean as a journalist a few weeks after the cleaning, the robot can already complete some other tasks—such as vacuuming and mopping—without any human help. If Tau succeeds in using all the data it is collecting to train truly autonomous cleaning robots, they could even become San Francisco’s newest tech tourist attraction as Waymos become more commonplace countrywide. [...] Tau Robotics still has a long way to go: The amount of data needed to train robots to do the varied and complicated tasks of apartment cleaning is probably enormous, and the company has completed only a couple hundred cleanings so far. But it’s remarkable that there are now humanoid robots able to clean your toilets and mop your floors, even if they need quite a bit of human help to do so. The Jetsons no longer feels quite so far away.

items.title: Inside App State’s Robotics Lab: Students explore the future of human–robot collaboration | Appalachian Today
items.summary:
Students work with a variety of robotic platforms, including robotic arms that handle objects, humanoid robots such as Pepper and NAO that are designed to interact with people and mobile robots that can move through an environment while manipulating objects. These platforms help students explore how robot behavior, movement and communication influence interactions with people. [...] Current lab projects focus on helping robots better understand and respond to the people around them. Researchers are investigating how robots can adapt their behavior over time, work safely alongside people and use different types of information to make more informed decisions.

One research area examines how robots can adjust their actions as people move nearby, an important challenge in workplaces where humans and robots share the same space. [...] This brief video offers a behind-the-scenes look at the Yeganeh Robotics (YeRo) Lab in App State’s College of Arts and Sciences. Demonstrations include a Go2 quadruped robot, often called a “robot dog,” navigating its surroundings while maintaining balance, and a robotic arm transferring an object between locations on a workbench. These examples illustrate the types of robotic systems and research questions student researchers are exploring in the lab.

items.title: Agility Robotics' Nasdaq debut invites scrutiny of humanoid robot market - Ars Technica
items.summary: Humanoid robots remain unproven at scale and have not yet achieved widespread commercialization, compared with industrial robots that have decades of proven track records in warehouses and factories. That frank acknowledgment is among the risks outlined in a securities filing by Agility Robotics—the first dedicated developer of humanoid robots to become a publicly traded company in the United States. [...] Beyond the challenges of building its own business, Agility’s financial disclosures also cautioned that “competition in the humanoid and robotics market is intensifying rapidly, with well-funded entrants including Boston Dynamics, Tesla, Apptronik, Figure AI, 1X Technologies, Sanctuary AI, Hexagon, and NEURA Robotics, among others, actively developing competing humanoid systems.” [...] In exchange for renting or purchasing the robots, customers would get access to the latest Agility robot known as Digit 5 starting in 2027. The bipedal robot has swappable end-effector “hands,” can lift up to 50-pound loads, and can perform more than 20 hours of work in a 24-hour period with the help of a fast-charging battery system.
